learning_outcomes.text: Model, analyze and calculate the static equilibrium of solids.
Analyze, describe and calculate the planar motion of particles and solids.
Know and apply the fundamentals of fluid statics and dynamics.
Identify, analyze and calculate oscillatory and wave phenomena.
Know and apply the fundamentals of thermodynamics.
Know the basic principles and laws governing heat transfer.
Know the general laws governing the behavior of electric and magnetic fields and apply them to problem solving.
Know, use and manipulate physical magnitudes appropriately and rigorously.
Is capable of performing experimental tests in the physics laboratory, as well as of analyzing, evaluating and interpreting the results obtained.
Is capable of working in a team, applying critical reasoning, making decisions, and communicating knowledge and conclusions in the field of industrial engineering.

teaching_methods: Classroom presentation of concepts and problem-solving sessions
assessment_rules: To pass the course by continuous evaluation, students must obtain a final grade equal to or greater than 5 after applying all stated percentages. For both ordinary and extraordinary calls, the exam consists of two parts, corresponding to each semester. Students may take only the pending parts (Blocks 1 and 2 or Blocks 3 and 4). Each exam part will represent 32% of the final evaluation, with the other continuous assessment grades retaining their original percentages.
